## Appearance

Uncle Jim is a tall, rather ungainly man with a somewhat stooped figure that nevertheless suggests great strength and endurance. He has a deeply lined, bronzed, and clean-shaven face framed by a thick mane of hair falling to his shoulders. His remarkably blue, deep-set eyes are clear and steady, appearing to twinkle or dream. Over time, he shows signs of aging, coming to appear frail and bent with noticeably grayer hair and a slightly trembling hand.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 CHAPTER 30 LESLIE DECIDES P3](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0003), [v4 CHAPTER 30 LESLIE DECIDES P11](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0011)_

## Personality

Captain Jim is a high-souled, simple-minded man possessing a rare and fine soul, with eternal youth in his eyes and heart. Known for his placid demeanor and invariable cheerfulness, he admits to having formed a habit of enjoying things and is a passionate worshipper of beauty. He is philosophical by nature, preferring to ponder all kinds of problems even if he cannot solve them. A born storyteller with a knack for bringing far-off things vividly to life, he also possesses a tolerable skill at playing his old brown fiddle. His single expressed fear is the horror of a lingering death.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 CHAPTER 8 MISS CORNELIA BRYANT COMES TO CALL P61](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0061), [v4 CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT FOUR WINDS POINT P5](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0005), [v4 CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT FOUR WINDS POINT P49](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0049), [v4 CHAPTER 14 NOVEMBER DAYS P3](../source/v04-c14.md#nw-v04-c14-p0003), [v4 CHAPTER 16 NEW YEAR’S EVE AT THE LIGHT P6](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0006), +4 more_

## History

Coming from a line of sea-going people, Captain Jim ran off to sea as a boy and spent a lifetime traveling the world, though his youth was marred when his sweetheart, [Margaret](../character/margaret.md), drowned at sea. Fifty years after her loss and five years after retiring from his life on the ocean, he lived at the [Four Winds Point](../codex/places.md#four-winds-point) lighthouse with his cat, the [First Mate](../character/first-mate.md). There he welcomed [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) to the community, quickly forming a close bond with [Anne](../character/anne.md) as a kindred spirit and introducing the couple to his collection of curios and true sea tales. Over the following months, Captain Jim frequently hosted [Anne](../character/anne.md), [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md), and their neighbor [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md), offering comfort to [Anne](../character/anne.md) when she grieved the loss of her newborn daughter, Joyce, and entrusting her with the story of his lost [Margaret](../character/margaret.md). He also shared his written journal of sea adventures with the [Blythes](../codex/factions.md#blythes), which led to an introduction to visiting author [Owen Ford](../character/owen-ford.md). Owen borrowed the life-book and agreed to write Captain Jim's life story combined with the tale of [Margaret](../character/margaret.md), drafting the manuscript at the lighthouse over the course of the summer. Later, when [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) discovered a medical possibility regarding Leslie's husband, Captain Jim lent [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) the money she needed to travel to [Montreal](../codex/places.md#montreal) for the procedure, and he was eventually honored when [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) named their newborn son, [James Matthew](../character/james-a.md), after him. Sometime after celebrating a [Liberal](../codex/factions.md#liberal) political victory, Captain Jim had a poignant conversation with [Anne](../character/anne.md) at the lighthouse, confiding his belief that his death was near and asking her to care for the [First Mate](../character/first-mate.md) when he was gone. After offering a warm benediction to [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) and Owen upon their engagement, Captain Jim was presented by [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) with the newly published copy of his life-book. The following morning, [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) saw the lighthouse light still burning after sunrise and entered to find that Captain Jim had peacefully passed away in his sleep with his published book resting on his chest.

_Sources: [v2 II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure P1](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0001), [v2 II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure P2](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0002), [v2 II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure P5](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0005), [v2 II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure P6](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0006), [v2 II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure P7](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0007), [v2 II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure P14](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0014), +668 more_

## Quotes

> "The Government don’t give lighthouse keepers such luxuries. Look at the colors that wood makes. If you’d like some driftwood for your fire, Mistress Blythe, I’ll bring you up a load some day. Sit down. I’m going to make you a cup of tea."
>
> — Uncle Jim — [v4 CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT FOUR WINDS POINT P24](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0024)

> "That’s Marshall Elliott—a mighty fine man with jest one streak of foolishness in him. I s’pose you wondered what his object was in turning himself into a sort of dime museum freak."
>
> — Uncle Jim — [v4 CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT FOUR WINDS POINT P32](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0032)

> "Come, now, Cornelia, I can’t see any harm in going to the Methodist church when there’s no preaching in your own. I’ve been a Presbyterian for seventy-six years, and it isn’t likely my theology will hoist anchor at this late day."
>
> — Uncle Jim — [v4 CHAPTER 15 CHRISTMAS AT FOUR WINDS P23](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0023)

> "I wanted to hear some good singing. The Methodists have a good choir; and you can’t deny, Cornelia, that the singing in our church is awful since the split in the choir."
>
> — Uncle Jim — [v4 CHAPTER 15 CHRISTMAS AT FOUR WINDS P25](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0025)

> "That’s just exactly the truth about Lewis Taylor. When I see those poor, miserable children of his, robbed of all children ought to have, it p’isens my own bite and sup for days afterwards."
>
> — Uncle Jim — [v4 CHAPTER 15 CHRISTMAS AT FOUR WINDS P47](../source/v04-c15.md#nw-v04-c15-p0047)
